subject: Request: Tailored uptime rider + evidence playbook for Aurelia Health
messages:
From: Maya Thompson <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: uptime rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Aurelia is enthusiastic about Redwood but Procurement has asked us to formalize a tailored uptime commitment and an evidence onboarding plan that maps to our operational audit needs. Specifically: 

- A 99.95% monthly uptime target for the dedicated model pool serving our workloads, with a regional failover carve-out.
- A latency SLO for the 95th percentile at <200ms for standard prompt lengths (<=512 tokens).
- An explicit evidence package: SOC2-type telemetry snapshots, weekly availability reports, incident postmortems for P1s, and a retention window for logs (365 days).

Can you provide a short addendum (SLA rider) and an ops evidence playbook we can attach to the MSA/SOW and reference in the order form? Also — what documentation will you provide for procurement and our security team to validate compliance during technical review?

I attached our standard procurement template and a short list of questions from Legal. Happy to coordinate a quick call if that’s easier.

Best,
Maya Thompson\Director, Procurement\Aurelia Health

Attachments: Aurelia_SLA_Request.pdf

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: Maya Thompson <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: uptime rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the template. I’m looping in Kimberly (legal lead for enterprise order forms) and Ben (solutions engineering) so we can give you an actionable addendum + evidence mapping.

High level next steps we propose:
1) We draft a short SLA rider (1-2 pages) that specifies: measured metric definitions (availability window & measurement method), the proposed 99.95% target, latency SLO language, and clear carve-outs for planned maintenance and regional failover.
2) We assemble an evidence playbook that maps each evidence item (SOC2-type telemetry snapshot, weekly availability CSV, P1 postmortem, log retention confirmation) to where it’s produced and how it will be shared.
3) We include an order-form clause referencing the addendum and a procurement acceptance checklist for signature via DocuSign.

Can you confirm: do you need continuous 365-day log access (e.g., read-only logs in a shared bucket) or just a signed attestation plus on-demand extracts? That will change how we describe operational access in the rider.

I’ll get a draft to you by EOD Wednesday in your timezone. If Legal prefers, we can route a ‘clean’ rider and also mark up a redlined MSA/SOW excerpt.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova\Senior Manager, Customer Success\Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: uptime rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Thanks for the loop. A few legal/contract items to cover in the draft rider: 

- Explicit measurement method: define availability as "successful response rate for accepted requests to the dedicated pool over UTC day, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure." State the sampling method and the monitoring endpoint (we usually cite our console telemetry and an internal synthetic probe).
- Remedies: define service credits schedule tied to monthly availability buckets (we can propose tiers: 99.95%+, 99.5–99.95%, <99.5%) — but ask Sales if credit caps are acceptable.
- Latency: for latency SLOs propose to scope to "typical production payloads (<=512 tokens) with no large attachments" and exclude batched bulk jobs.
- Evidence: we can provide weekly availability exports, per-incident summaries, and a SOC2 summary report; we do not publish raw PII logs — redaction/filtered extracts only. We need clarity from Aurelia on whether they require feed-level KV caches or raw request logs.

Ben, can you enumerate what artifacts we can promise in an onboarding playbook (synthetic probe setup, runbook link, sample weekly CSV, sample postmortem template)? Marcus — FYI on regional failover language; if they want a contractual cross-region fallback we’ll need a capacity reservation or a defined burst allowance in the order form.

-kim

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: uptime rider + evidence for enterprise MSA

Kim — list below are the standard artifacts we can commit to and how we will deliver them in the evidence playbook: 

- Weekly availability CSV (UTC date, total accepted requests, successful responses, availability %) — auto-export from console; shared via SFTP or a Google Drive folder.
- Synthetic probe graphs and raw probe output for a 30-day rolling window — console access to read-only dashboards or exported PNG/CSV.
- Incident timeline + postmortem template for P1 events — we can share redacted postmortems and a timeline document.
- SOC2 Type II summary and auditor letter — downloadable PDF; full SOC2 reports require an NDA/controlled access request.
- Log retention confirmation: we retain telemetry and operational traces for 365 days; raw request payloads are available only as redacted extracts on request and require procurement/legal approval.
- Latency measurement: we can produce p95 latency over the same rolling period with payload size annotation.

For the order form: to support regional failover commitments we recommend adding a short clause that commits to a baseline burst capacity in region B for the first 8 weeks post-cutover, and then a scalable burst policy thereafter. That lets us offer a stronger contractual fallback without immediate reserved additional capacity. Marcus — I’ll need the exact phrasing you want for the burst allowance.

-Ben

From: Maya Thompson <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: legal@aureliahealth.com
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Tailored uptime rider + evidence playbook for Aurelia Health

Sofia, Kimberly, Ben — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before you draft: 

1) Log access: Aurelia requires on-demand access to redacted request extracts for incident investigations; we do not need continuous read access to raw PII. The extracts should include timestamps, request id, model id, and token counts.
2) Remedies: Procurement prefers a three-tier credit schedule (we can accept your proposed bands) and a 30% cap on credits per month. 3) Regional failover: we are okay with an initial 8-week burst allowance as a probationary period; please include a clause that defines acceptable performance degradation thresholds during failover and the notification SLA for invoking failover.

If you can send the rider + playbook draft today, Legal will triage and return markup within 48 hours. If it helps, we can provision a short 30-minute call Thursday to run through redline items.

Best,
Maya

Attachments: Aurelia_SLA_Request.pdf (resend)
